as.sfi_dedup_instructions: Deduplicate only when candidates represent the same source-backed SFI under the same configured semantic identity scope. Apply these identity scopes: Content Domain is scoped by Class; Chapter is scoped by Class and Content Domain; NCERT Learning Outcome is scoped by Class only; Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome and Indicator are scoped by Class, Content Domain, and Chapter. Class IX and Class X are always distinct scopes because LO, CLO, and C numbering restarts in Class X. Merge repeated Class values within the document. Merge Content Domain values only within the same Class, including non-contiguous repeats such as Class IX 'World of living' returning for Chapter 13. Merge Chapter candidates only within the same Class, Content Domain, and canonical chapter identity. For the uncoded Class, Content Domain, and Chapter organizer types, candidates with the same canonical_statement_value_key and the same configured identity scope represent one logical organizer under this runtime policy and must not be left as multiple eligible singleton groups. If the bounded source evidence instead establishes genuinely distinct organizers that the configured no-code identity fields cannot distinguish, return conflict or needs_review rather than producing colliding mintable groups. Within one Class, repeated NCERT LO occurrences with the same LO code normally represent one class-level LO even when examples are shortened, punctuation differs, or minor source typos occur; merge them only when their core learning-outcome semantics are compatible. Preserve every occurrence as provenance. Do not merge any of the four known code/text conflict occurrences with the ordinary same-code LO group: Class IX Chapter 2 LO16 carrying LO12 text; Class IX Chapter 12 LO6 carrying LO7 text; Class X Chapter 6 LO14 carrying Class IX LO14 text; Class X Chapter 10 LO9 carrying Class IX LO9 text. Each confirmed anomalous occurrence is a complete source-visible item: place it in its own keep_separate singleton so it remains mintable as a source-faithful same-code/different-content SFI with audit evidence. Use conflict or needs_review only when the bounded evidence does not establish a complete distinct source occurrence. CLO# and C# codes are unique only within a Class. Merge overlap/repeated-extraction copies when identity scope, statement_type, normalized code, complete wording, and provenance are compatible. Keep the same CLO or C code across Class IX and Class X separate. Do not merge different statement_type values merely because candidates share wording, code, row, or surrounding context. The only permitted cross-type merge is the pipeline's narrow same_source_occurrence_cross_type case: all candidates must preserve one identical non-empty exact description_source_anchors set for the same physical source occurrence, their shared scope dimensions must not conflict, and the source must clearly support one canonical statement type. In that case, merge the duplicate extractions and select the existing candidate whose classification is source-correct; otherwise use keep_separate, conflict, or needs_review. In particular, never merge a genuine CLO with a genuine Indicator even when their wording is identical, and never merge different codes solely because descriptions match. Known exact-text/different-code examples such as Class IX CLO15 versus CLO19, Class IX C40 versus C48, Class IX C126 versus C145, and Class X C188 versus C209 must remain separate. Same-code/different-content within one scope should be keep_separate when each variant is a complete source-visible occurrence; use conflict or needs_review only when identity or source support is genuinely unresolved. Source-visible table rows, configured identity scope, Chapter context, and statement type outrank lexical similarity.
as.sfi_extraction_instructions: Scope extraction to Section 9, 'Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes and Indicators.' The only block-level SFIs in scope are the source-visible '9.1 Class IX' and '9.2 Class X' headings. From the two Section 9 standards tables, extract Class, Content Domain, and Chapter as Standard Grouping records; extract NCERT Learning Outcome (LO#), Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome (CLO#), and Indicator (C#) as Standard records. NCERT LOs and CLOs are learning expectations, not organizational groupings. Treat the table headers and all 'Key concepts' prose as context only, not as SFIs. When the first table cell contains a domain, a chapter label, and Key concepts prose, emit separate candidates only for the visible domain label and complete chapter label; do not include Key concepts prose in either description. In cells containing multiple coded statements, emit one candidate per complete visible code-statement pair in source order. Preserve the exact source-language wording, punctuation, spelling, and visible code; place the normalized code in statement_code and keep the separately represented code out of description. Do not combine multiple CLOs or indicators merely because they share a physical table row. Combine fragments only when one coded statement visibly continues across adjacent cited cells or rows. Codes restart in Class X: LO#, CLO#, and C# identity is always class-scoped. Populate the configured Class identity scope and code scope from the active Class context. When Class is not explicit in the current raw table rows, use source_context.section_path_recent_first and select the nearest compatible Class heading: '9.1 Class IX' for the first standards table and '9.2 Class X' for the second. The Class X table context may also contain the older '9.1 Class IX' heading; do not skip the nearer '9.2 Class X' entry for that stale heading. Section context establishes scope only: it must not create or anchor a Class candidate unless the Class heading itself is the target source-visible block. Do not infer parentage from numeric code ranges because C and CLO numbers do not encode their parents. Do not extract Section 5 curricular expectations, the Section 6 content-domain overview, the Section 8 master LO tables, cognitive-level examples, front matter, explanatory narrative, pedagogy, assessment material, or any other non-Section-9 content. Do not correct source errors during extraction. Preserve visible source evidence. Four confirmed code/text conflicts must retain the printed code and printed wording and receive a concise extraction note: (1) Class IX Chapter 2 shows LO16 with the Class IX LO12 daily-life statement; (2) Class IX Chapter 12 Sound shows LO6 with the Class IX LO7 labelled-diagrams statement; (3) Class X Chapter 6 Life Processes shows LO14 with Class IX LO14 wording; and (4) Class X Chapter 10 Light shows LO9 with Class IX LO9 wording. Do not infer a candidate from section_path or helper-only filldown/rowspan context; a grouping or standard must be visible in the raw block, header, or body-row source content. Every complete coded statement independently printed in a different source body row is a separate extraction occurrence, even when its statement type, code, and wording exactly match another row in the same window. Never combine such independently printed occurrences into one candidate. Combine table_row_indexes only when one coded statement is visibly split across adjacent rows or cells and the later row does not independently print a complete code-statement pair. Section 9 repeatedly prints class-level NCERT Learning Outcomes beside different chapter/CLO mappings; preserve each printed LO occurrence as its own candidate and leave logical merging of repeated occurrences to SFI deduplication. In particular, Class IX LO1 printed in source rows 1 and 5 and Class X LO3 printed in source rows 2 and 6 must each be emitted as two separate occurrence candidates.
as.sfi_extraction_validation_instructions: Independently verify complete source-faithful extraction from the supplied Section 9 window. Class, Content Domain, and Chapter must be Standard Grouping; NCERT Learning Outcome, Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome, and Indicator must be Standard. Ensure every visible LO#, CLO#, and C# statement in the selected raw rows is represented exactly once unless one statement visibly continues across cited adjacent rows; split cells that contain multiple coded statements. For every coded candidate, require the candidate's own source_text and cited table rows to contain that exact raw code directly paired with the complete description. Do not borrow a code or wording from another statement in the same window. Descriptions and source_text must preserve source spelling, punctuation, grammar, and capitalization; do not silently repair errors such as 'plants and plants', wording drift, or malformed grammar. Verify the configured Class identity scope and code scope from the active source context when Class is not explicit in the raw table rows. Use source_context.section_path_recent_first in order and select the first compatible Class heading; for the second standards table, the nearer '9.2 Class X' entry must outrank the older carried '9.1 Class IX' entry. Treat section_path_recent_first as context-only scope evidence: it cannot create a candidate or supply description, source_text, or anchors. Treat Key concepts, table headers used only as column labels, section_path_recent_first, filldown, and rowspan helper context as non-quotable context. Use the detailed Section 9 tables as authoritative for chapter numbering and titles. In Class IX the order is Chapter 8 Motion, Chapter 9 Force & Laws of Motion, Chapter 10 Gravitation, Chapter 11 Work and Energy, Chapter 12 Sound, and Chapter 13 Why do we fall ill?; do not import the conflicting Section 6 overview numbering. Recognize four confirmed source code/text conflicts and preserve them exactly rather than rewriting the code: (1) Class IX Chapter 2 shows LO16 with the Class IX LO12 daily-life statement; (2) Class IX Chapter 12 Sound shows LO6 with the Class IX LO7 labelled-diagrams statement; (3) Class X Chapter 6 Life Processes shows LO14 with Class IX LO14 wording; (4) Class X Chapter 10 Light shows LO9 with Class IX LO9 wording. When one of these appears, retain the visible code and exact visible statement as a candidate and add a concise extraction note identifying the source inconsistency. Reject candidates sourced from Section 8, Section 6, front matter, narrative, cognitive examples, pedagogy, or assessment content. Reject any candidate that combines two or more non-contiguous body rows when each cited row independently contains a complete printed code-statement pair. Identical code and wording do not make separately printed rows one extraction occurrence. For Section 9 repeated class-level NCERT LOs, require one candidate per printed row occurrence and leave logical consolidation to deduplication. Specifically, Class IX LO1 in source rows 1 and 5 and Class X LO3 in source rows 2 and 6 must remain separate candidates.
as.sfi_has_child_instructions: Resolve the Section 9 source hierarchy as a DAG, not a single linear tree. StandardsFramework directly parents Class. Class directly parents its Content Domain nodes and its class-level NCERT Learning Outcome nodes. Content Domain directly parents Chapter. Chapter directly parents the CLOs visible under that chapter. Source-visible Content Domain and Chapter cells that row-span into later rows remain the active structural parents for the rows they cover; an explicit later cell overrides carried context. A CLO also has each corresponding NCERT LO as an additional direct parent when the table explicitly maps one or more LOs to the CLO in the same raw row or through a source-visible row span or continued row group. When an LO cell originates in an earlier raw row but visibly spans into the CLO row, select that LO endpoint even if the finalized LO and CLO preserve different table_row_indexes. Use rowspan or filldown helper context only to interpret this structural carryover, never as a substitute for a source-visible parent SFI. Shared row, table, segment, window, source_context, or source-order evidence is retrieval context, not proof that a row span or continued-row mapping exists. Claim a row-span or continuation mapping only when the bounded request explicitly supports it; when the supplied wording, scope, source order, and evidence do not identify the correct LO safely, mark the CLO unresolved rather than selecting a nearby or same-code substitute. An Indicator normally has one direct source-visible CLO parent. Select multiple CLO parents only when the bounded source evidence clearly presents the same Indicator as jointly supporting multiple CLOs; never infer multiple parents merely because several CLOs and Indicators share a row, segment, or window. Do not create hasChild edges from Key concepts prose, table headers, Section 6 overview content, or Section 8 master-table occurrences. For a raw row or source-visible row-spanned or continued row group containing multiple CLOs and indicators, shared table context narrows the parent set but does not mean every indicator belongs to every CLO; select the semantically matching direct CLO using the visible statements and contiguous row grouping. Use the detailed Section 9 chapter structure as authoritative. For Class IX, Motion is Chapter 8, Force & Laws of Motion is Chapter 9, Gravitation is Chapter 10, Work and Energy is Chapter 11, Sound is Chapter 12, and Why do we fall ill? is Chapter 13. Class IX 'World of living' is non-contiguous and resumes at Chapter 13; explicit current table-cell context outranks the previously active domain. The Class X table's cumulative section_path may contain both '9.1 Class IX' and '9.2 Class X'; treat '9.2 Class X' and the later table segment as the active scope. Never attach Class X records to Class IX because of stale section-path carryover. Do not infer parents from numeric C/CLO ranges or code similarity. For same-code/different-content NCERT LO records, including the four confirmed source anomalies, keep endpoints distinct and select the source-local LO whose preserved description matches the LO wording printed in the CLO's row. When the anomalous LO endpoint from that row is supplied, prefer it over the ordinary same-code LO; do not attach the CLO to another LO merely because the normalized code matches. Retain the Chapter parent as well. Prefer exact same-row evidence, source-visible row-span or continuation evidence, same-table evidence, explicit domain/chapter cells, source_context_key, and local Class scope over nearby or stale headings. Use the StandardsFramework root only for Class nodes or when no supplied source-supported parent exists.
as.sfi_has_child_validation_instructions: Independently audit every Section 9 direct-parent decision against the supplied child context and bounded parent candidates. Enforce this source DAG: StandardsFramework directly parents Class; Class directly parents Content Domain and class-level NCERT Learning Outcome; Content Domain directly parents Chapter; Chapter directly parents Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome; each CLO also has the source-mapped NCERT Learning Outcome parent or parents; and each Indicator directly parents to its semantically corresponding source-supported CLO or CLOs. For every CLO, require both its source-visible Chapter parent and every source-supported corresponding NCERT LO parent when those endpoints are supplied. Reject a draft that selects only the Chapter or only the NCERT LO when the complete supported parent set is available. Do not infer all-to-all mappings merely because multiple LOs, CLOs, or Indicators share a raw row or continued row group; use the visible statements and contiguous source structure to select only the corresponding endpoints. For an Indicator, require every clearly supported CLO parent when the bounded evidence shows genuine joint support, but reject multiple CLO parents based only on co-location. Validate LO-to-CLO mapping from exact source-local wording and any explicitly supplied row-span or continuation evidence. An LO originating in an earlier row may be the correct parent even when the finalized LO and CLO preserve different table_row_indexes, but helper-only rowspan or filldown context cannot invent a parent SFI. Do not treat shared row, table, segment, window, source_context, or source order as explicit proof of a row span or continuation, and reject any draft whose rationale claims source structure that is not present in the bounded request. If the required source-supported endpoint is absent from the bounded candidate set, or the supplied evidence cannot identify it safely, mark the child unresolved rather than selecting a nearby, same-code, or semantically similar substitute. For the four confirmed source anomalies—Class IX Chapter 2 LO16 with LO12 wording; Class IX Chapter 12 LO6 with LO7 wording; Class X Chapter 6 LO14 with Class IX LO14 wording; and Class X Chapter 10 LO9 with Class IX LO9 wording—select the anomalous source-local LO endpoint when it is supplied. Do not replace it with the ordinary same-code endpoint or with a different-code endpoint that merely shares copied wording. Retain the Chapter parent as well. Explicit current Content Domain and Chapter cells override carried context. Treat Class IX 'World of living' as resuming at Chapter 13. For Class X, the current '9.2 Class X' context and later table segment override stale '9.1 Class IX' labels. Use the detailed Section 9 chapter numbering and titles rather than the conflicting Section 6 overview. Reject a resolved StandardsFramework-root parent for any non-Class child, and reject unresolved root fallback when a defensible complete semantic parent set is supplied. Never infer parentage from C/CLO numeric ranges or code similarity.

lc.generation_instructions:
Generate Learning Components only from finalized `Indicator` SFIs. Do not generate skills from Class, Content Domain, Chapter, NCERT Learning Outcome, or Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome records, nor from Key concepts prose, introductory rationale, pedagogy notes, or assessment guidance.

Indicators in this source are already verb-led, measurable, leaf-level expectations ('Explains the need for a stream of electrons and a conductor.'), so most yield exactly one cleanly restated skill. Split when one Indicator states several independently teachable actions, or several distinct objects or aspects such as 'the structure and functions of X'; this source signals the action case with coordinated verbs ('Prepares stained temporary mounts of onion peel and human cheek cells, records observations, and draws labelled diagrams.') or with an explicit list of distinct experiments ('Conducts the following experiments and states the type of reaction: - action of water on quicklime, action of heat on ferrous sulphate crystals, ...'). Never split on a slash alternation: CBSE writes interchangeable alternatives with '/' ('digestive/ circulatory/ excretory system', 'diagrams/flow charts/ maps'), and that is one skill offered in variants, not several skills.

Enumerations of content carry scope and must stay bound to the skill they qualify, whether parenthesised ('(Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma)', '(forebrain, mid brain, hind brain)') or inline, as must SI units, quantities, chemical formulae, named laws, and organism, material, and hormone names. Drop only the parentheticals that carry no learning content: NCERT source pointers ('(Refer activity 3.10 in NCERT)'), modality qualifiers ('(Theoretically and experimentally)', '(Both textually and through observations)'), and long '(e.g. ...)' illustrations of hypothetical situations.

Practical and investigative Indicators ('Conducts an experiment to make esters using alcohol and carboxylic acid', 'Plans and conducts investigations to verify the phenomenon of diffusion and osmosis') state the skill itself rather than a suggested classroom activity, so restate them as skills instead of discarding them. Disposition Indicators ('Exhibits objectivity and rational thinking while approaching discussions on puberty and sex in peer groups.', 'Takes steps to conserve the environment...') must keep their disposition meaning and must never be converted into a measurable task.

Where an Indicator is stated abstractly, use its ancestor path for disambiguation only: the parent Content Domain Specific Learning Outcome first, then the Chapter and the NCERT Learning Outcome that CLO maps to. Add nothing those ancestors and the Indicator do not state together. The leading `C#` code is an identifier, not content, and its numbering restarts in Class X; never treat it as decomposition input. Class applicability is carried in the SFI identity scope ('Class IX', 'Class X'), so do not restate the class inside skill text. Preserve CBSE and NCERT science terminology, the source's British spellings, and Indian contextual references. Output skills in English.
